content.content: The checkout service runs on ECS Fargate in ap-south-1.
The payments database is Postgres 16 on RDS with a read replica.
Redis is used for session storage and rate limiting.
The retry policy for outbound webhooks uses exponential backoff.
Feature flags are managed in LaunchDarkly.
The staging environment mirrors production at a quarter of the capacity.
Deploys go out through GitHub Actions on merge to main.
The API gateway enforces a 30 second request timeout.
Background jobs run on Celery with RabbitMQ as the broker.
Observability is Grafana dashboards on top of Prometheus.
The search index is OpenSearch, reindexed nightly.
Object storage is S3 with lifecycle rules moving old objects to Glacier.
A checkout outage in February was caused by connection pool exhaustion.
The March incident review recommended adding circuit breakers.
An earlier retry storm doubled load on the payments service.
The team postponed the Kafka migration to next quarter.
A memory leak in the notification worker was fixed by upgrading the SDK.
The load test in July peaked at 4K requests per second.
Priya leads the platform team.
Karthik reviews all database migrations.
Sneha manages the on-call rotation.
Vikram works on the mobile client.
The design system is maintained by Ananya.
Meera is the product manager for checkout.
Code review requires one approval before merge.
Migrations must be backwards compatible for one release.
The team writes runbooks for every alert.
Documentation lives in the docs directory of each repository.
Secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager, never in environment files.
Type hints are required on all new Python code.
Line length is capped at 100 characters.
Dependency updates are batched weekly.
Local development uses Docker Compose.
Dependencies are managed with uv.
Linting is ruff, formatting is ruff format.
Type checking is mypy in strict mode.
The monorepo is split into services and packages directories.
Terraform manages all cloud infrastructure.
Alerting routes through PagerDuty.
The changelog is generated from conventional commit messages.
Rohan is on-call and works at Nimbus, focusing on payments.
The user writes tests in pytest.
Commit messages are kept conventional by the user.
